answer: A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Policies are written in cipher, settled in ocean, and oasis lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 36% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. That bill is paid per identity, so 35 aliases cost 144 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
